card.description: A movie studio has facts about 186 real movies that came out in US theaters from 2022 to 2026. Each record is one movie. The label says if the movie was a box office hit (Yes) or not (No). A hit earned much more than it cost to make. You can also choose Critics Liked It or Rating as the label.
card.source: Real movies and real facts from Wikipedia, The Numbers and Box Office Mojo, collected in November 2026. A box office hit earned at least 2.5 times its budget (the money spent to make it) around the world. Critics Liked It means a Rotten Tomatoes critics score of 75% or higher. We picked which movies to include: G, PG and PG-13 movies that played in many theaters.

context.potentialUses: Use the tree to predict whether a new movie might earn much more than it cost to make.
context.potentialMisuses: The tree is trained on only 167 movies from five years. We only picked G, PG and PG-13 movies, so it may predict poorly for R-rated movies. Movies from August to October 2026 were still in theaters, so some of their box office numbers may change. A movie can earn a lot of money and still not be good. You might not like it.

fields.description: What year did the movie come out in US theaters?
What kind of story is the movie?
Where did the movie's story come from?
Is the movie a sequel or a later part of a movie series?
Is the movie a new version of an older movie?
Is the movie about a superhero?
Do the characters sing songs as part of the story?
How long is the movie? Short is under 100 minutes. Long is 130 minutes or more.
What season did the movie come out?
How much did the movie cost to make? Low is under $50 million. High is $150 million or more.
What letter grade did people give the movie after they saw it on opening weekend?
Did movie critics like it? Yes means a Rotten Tomatoes critics score of 75% or higher.
What is the movie's US age rating (G, PG or PG-13)?
Did the movie earn at least 2.5 times its budget around the world? This is what the tree predicts for each movie.
